messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I ran the new quantized embed (heron-lite int6) on the short-query holdout and saw a 3.6% drop in recall@10 vs fp16. Putting this here in case it's noisy or reproducible.

alex: Repro steps: `./eval_embed.sh --model heron-lite-int6 --dataset short_holdout --batch-size 32 --seed 42 --metric recall@10`

alex: Raw numbers (one run): fp16: 0.742 recall@10 | int6: 0.715 recall@10

chloe: ouch. did you try different seeds / batch sizes? sometimes microbatch ordering changes results with quant rounding.

alex: Not yet. Tried batch-size 32 and 64, both similar drop. Seed 42 only.

sam: two quick hypotheses: (1) prefix/kvcache warmup difference with batching, (2) numeric instability in the quant kernel on short sequences.

maria: can you paste the eval command and the exact quant config? e.g., per-channel vs per-tensor, clamp strategy, scale method.

alex: quant config: `--quant-mode int6 --per-channel true --clamp linear --symmetric false`

alex: eval command: ```bash
./eval_embed.sh --model heron-lite-int6 \
  --dataset short_holdout \
  --batch-size 32 \
  --seed 42 \n  --normalize true \n  --num-workers 4
```

chloe: try `--batch-size 1` and `--batch-size 128` and compare cosine histograms. if distribution shifts, it's ordering/accum issue. also try `--per-channel false` to check config sensitivity.

eval-bot: CI artifact uploaded: https://ci.redwood/embeds/1746500001/artifacts (contains logits.csv, cos_hist_{bs}.png, eval_summary.json) :package:

alex: uploaded initial histograms to the artifact link. quick look: int6 histogram mean cosine is ~0.81 vs fp16 ~0.83 (short queries). tails are heavier on int6 (more low-sim pairs).

sam: heavier tails align with rounding noise increasing orthogonality for near neighbors. try running cosine with high-precision post-normalize: compute embeddings in int6 path, cast to float64 before normalize and distance — to see if normalization numerics are causing it.

maria: also run with deterministic dataloader: `--shuffle false --seed 0 --num-workers 0` — rules out asynchronous prefetch ordering.

alex: ok re-running now with: batch sizes [1,32,128], per-channel false, shuffle false, seed 1 and 7. will drop results in a sec.

alex: Results (quick summary):
- bs=1, seed=1: int6 recall@10 0.734 (fp16 0.742)
- bs=32, seed=1: int6 0.715 (fp16 0.742)
- bs=128, seed=1: int6 0.718 (fp16 0.741)
- bs=32, seed=7: int6 0.719
- per-channel=false, bs=32: int6 0.738

chloe: interesting. per-channel=false reducing drop => per-channel quantization might be the suspect. that narrows it down.

sam: agreed. per-channel often more sensitive to short-sequence statistics if scale estimation uses small group samples. how are scales computed? per-layer running min/max, or per-bucket?

alex: current scale: per-channel computed from calibration on 1k samples (default). scale-estimate uses percentile 99.9 to avoid outliers.

maria: can you try calibrating per-channel on larger sample (10k) and with different percentile (99.0)? if per-channel scales are noisy, that could skew nearest neighbors.

alex: trying calib-size 10k and pct=99.0 now.

alex: New run: per-channel=true, calib-size=10000, pct=99.0, bs=32 -> int6 recall@10 0.735 (fp16 0.742)

chloe: good improvement. suggests scale estimation noise is amplifying quant error and hurting recall.

sam: actionable: for onboarding, require per-channel calibration sample >=10k or fall back to per-tensor if data volume small. also add a calibration stability check in the onboarding CI (run 3 calib random seeds and report stddev of recall@k).

maria: agree. also add a quick cosine-delta check: sample 1k pairs of top-1 neighbors in fp16, measure delta in cos under quant config; if >X% pairs drop below threshold, flag.

alex: i'll prepare a small PR with: (1) calibration-size default bump to 10k for per-channel, (2) CI stability check (3 seeds), (3) diagnostic histogram + cosine-delta report artifact.

alex: PR draft: https://git.redwood/embeddings/pull/983 (wip)

chloe: thanks. can you add a short note in the model onboarding checklist: "if per-channel quant used, require calib-size >= 10k or prefer per-tensor"?

alex: will do.

sam: one more note — document that short-query cohorts (len <=16 tokens) are more sensitive; add them to default holdout for embed onboarding.

maria: i can run an extended sweep tomorrow across more holdouts (multilang short queries + code snippets).

alex: awesome. thanks everyone. i'll follow up in the PR with artifacts and a summary. :thumbsup:
